To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the iscoms prepared from the tegumental antigents of Echinococcuss granulosus protocolex induce a strong immune response in mice when given by the intranasal and parenteral routes.
the i.n. immunization with E. granulosus tegumental antigents in iscoms induces a strong mucosal and systemic immune response, biased to carbohydrate epitopes.
the intranasal administration of E. granulosus iscoms is an immunization route that can be considered as an alternative to the subcutaneous one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new vaccine for hydatid disease.
the use of Echinococcal iscoms as a vaccine for the control of hydatidosis.
the development of a new vaccine against echinococcosis, based on iscom technology, which may have an advantage over other vaccines because of its potential use in mucosal administration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the i.n. route is more efficient for the induction of mucosal and systemic immune responses than the s.c., and this is particularly true for glycosylated antigens.
the iscoms are a good candidate as vaccine for Echinococcus infection, and the intranasal route of immunization may be the most appropriate for the induction of a strong mucosal immune response.
iscoms are a suitable adjuvant to induce mucosal and systemic immunity to E. granulosus antigens, but that the i.n. route is not as effective as the s.c. protocol in terms of IgG production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
i.n. immunization with iscom‐encapsulated antigens of E. granulosus is a useful strategy for the induction of protective immunity.

the i.n. route induces a mucosal and systemic immune response with a bias towards carbohydrate epitopes and IgA antibodies, while the parenteral route induces a systemic immune response, with a bias towards protein epitopes and IgG antibodies.
the i.n. administration of iscoms induces a strong immune response with a mucosal bias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
i.n. immunization with E. granulosus surface iscoms is a good alternative to parenteral immunization.
i.n. immunization with iscom‐formulated antigens may be a useful tool to induce protective immunity against helminthic infections.
the i.n. route is a useful alternative for the immunization with Echinococus granulosus tegumental antigends, and that it may be useful in the development of a vaccine against echinococcosis.
